reconstructed_theorem_text: For every complete real inner-product space E, every function f:E→ℝ, every curve X:ℝ→E, every point z∈E, and every real number T>0, assume f is continuously Fréchet differentiable on E, z is a global minimizer of f (f(z)≤f(x) for every x∈E), X is continuous on [0,T], and for every t∈[0,T) the right derivative of X at t exists and equals −∇f(X(t)). Then there exists s∈[0,T] such that ‖∇f(X(s))‖≤‖∇f(X(u))‖ for every u∈[0,T], and ‖∇f(X(s))‖≤√((f(X(0))−f(z))/T). The square root is the nonnegative real square root, and its argument is nonnegative by global minimality and T>0.
objects: E: arbitrary complete real inner-product space (possibly infinite-dimensional)

domains.X: all real times, with regularity assumptions only on the specified interval

quantifiers: Universal over E and its normed additive group, real inner-product and completeness structures, f, X, z and T; universal right-derivative condition over t∈[0,T); existential s after all hypotheses; universal u∈[0,T] in the minimizing property.
assumptions: For all t∈[0,T), the derivative within [t,∞) at t is −∇f(X(t))
conclusion: There is an attained minimum of the gradient norm along the closed trajectory segment, and at a minimizing time the gradient norm is at most the square root of the initial function-value gap divided by T.
scopes: No derivative condition is imposed at T.
The right-derivative condition is imposed at 0.
The minimizing time may be an endpoint.
No convexity, Lipschitz gradient, finite-dimensionality, or uniqueness of the curve is assumed.
This is a bound at an existential minimizing time, not a bound at every time or specifically at terminal time T.
The theorem assumes a trajectory with these properties; it does not assert existence of such a trajectory or a global minimizer.
constant_dependencies: The explicit bound depends only on f(X(0))−f(z) and T, with coefficient 1 under the square root and no dimension-dependent constant.
